identity.name: Mixed acetic and tartaric acid esters of mono- and diglycerides of fatty acids
synonyms: Mixed acetic and tartaric acid esters of mono- and diglycerides
TARTARIC, ACETIC and FATTY ACID ESTERS of GLYCEROL, mixed
identity.chemical_class: Mixed acetic/tartaric acid esters of glycerol mono- and diglycerides (glycerol ester emulsifier mixture)

function.mechanism: Amphiphilic glycerol-fatty-acid esters reduce oil-water interfacial tension and stabilize emulsions.

adi.basis: EFSA 2025 abstract reports E472f exposure below an ADI of 600 mg/kg bw/day; this follows the 2020 EFSA group ADI framework for E472d/e/f expressed as tartaric acid.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA reported E472f dietary exposure below ADI in assessed scenarios; technical data were insufficient to support a proposed specification amendment for E472f, but no exposure-based safety concern was identified.

fda.cfr_citation: No explicit E472f entry found in 21 CFR Title 21 XML (2026-02-19); related DATEM listings at 21 CFR 184.1101 and 21 CFR 582.4101

adi.basis: JECFA mixed tartaric/acetic entry (Chemical 3714) shows ADI WITHDRAWN (evaluation year 2001); comment states specifications were merged with DATEM, whose separate entry shows ADI 0-50 mg/kg bw.

concerns.summary: A large prospective cohort reported positive associations between higher intake of some emulsifier groups including E471/E472 and cardiovascular outcomes; observational design limits causal inference for E472f.
A prospective cohort reported associations between several emulsifier intakes and cancer outcomes, but this was not E472f-specific evidence.
Mouse data showed metabolic and microbiome disruption for common emulsifiers including mono-/diglycerides as a class; this does not isolate E472f.
Regulatory uncertainty exists because JECFA's additive-specific mixed tartaric/acetic entry is withdrawn, while EFSA maintains ADI-based risk conclusions for current use scenarios.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2020 reported no adverse effects relevant for humans for E472a-f and no safety concern at reported uses/use levels.
EFSA 2025 reported E472f exposure estimates below ADI across assessed population groups/scenarios.
No IARC Monographs classification entry was identified for E472f/name variants in the current IARC classifications dataset.

populations: general population groups assessed by EFSA
adi_exceedance.notes: In the consulted EFSA 2025 abstract, E472f exposures were below the ADI of 600 mg/kg bw/day in assessed scenarios.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory evidence specific to E472f is primarily EFSA 2020/2025 and indicates exposure below ADI with no identified exposure-driven safety concern at reported uses. Uncertainty remains due the withdrawn additive-specific JECFA entry and lack of modern E472f-specific human toxicology, while newer concern signals are largely emulsifier-class and indirect.
key_factors: EFSA ADI framework includes E472f and 2025 exposure estimates are below ADI
EFSA 2025 flagged insufficient technical support for proposed E472f specification amendment, but did not identify exposure-based safety concern
No explicit E472f listing found in current FDA Title 21 XML; related DATEM entries are GRAS with GMP conditions
JECFA additive-specific mixed tartaric/acetic entry shows ADI withdrawn and merged to DATEM context
No IARC classification entry found for E472f or close name variants
Recent safety signals come from indirect emulsifier-class epidemiology/animal studies
